newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan seeks active U.S. role to push peace - PM.
newsitem.headline: Jordan seeks active U.S. role to push peace - PM.

text.p: Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali said on Saturday his country sought a more active U.S. role to reactivate stalled Middle East peace.
Majali said King Hussein had lobbied for more U.S. action in talks with President Bill Clinton during a visit to the United States. The monarch returned to Jordan on Friday.

"King Hussein was asking from the United States not to play a role of a soft enthusiast and supporter; but as partners they have to be more active to present all the solutions which allow the two sides (Israeli and Palestinian) to continue the peace process," Majali said in his first news conference since taking office as prime minister in March.

Israeli-Palestinian tensions have spilled into street battles in the West Bank since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent bulldozers last month to start work on a Jewish settlement on an East Jerusalem hill.

"It's critical (tension in Middle East peace) but I do not think it is bad..I do not think it will stay like this for long," Majali said. "I am a very optimistic person so I think every problem has a solution and there will be a solution to restart the peace process."
He said Jordan believed Washington was working on "concrete ideas which hopefully will restart the peace process."
President Bill Clinton met Netanyahu last week to propose U.S. ideas for starting talks.
